evidence.s1_requirements: Every requirement in steps/1.md is met. snapshot() returns {version, root} built from plain per-node objects. The test helper resumeAt asserts deepEqual(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(snapshot)), snapshot) (step1.patch:2224-2225). BehaviourTreeSnapshot (and NodeSnapshot) are exported from src/index.ts (step1.patch:1750). restore() puts the tree in the same state, so it makes the same agent calls and reaches the same result; resumeAt checks this in lockstep at every possible snapshot point and per node type. The snapshot keeps node states, children, repeat/retry target and current counts (Repeat.ts:99-116), lotto selectedChild (Lotto.ts:73-87) and wait totalDuration/waitedDuration (Wait.ts:111-133). The remaining wait time is honoured in both time modes (tests at step1.patch:2462-2502). A finished tree restores as finished and draws random numbers again on the next step (step1.patch:2415-2449). The README has the API and an example (step1.patch:9-60).
evidence.s1_correctness: Each node type saves exactly the state that its onUpdate reads. Composite and Decorator recurse into children. Lotto saves the index of the picked child, or null when a guard resolved it before it picked one (fix commit 1576e15; validation in BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts hasValidData). In clock mode, Wait computes waitedDuration at snapshot time and restore sets initialUpdateTime = now - waited; in delta mode the stored waitedDuration is kept. Action keeps a settled but unhandled promise result as a string, and the original tree's error message stringifies it the same way. The new updatePromiseId ignores stale promises after a restore. Lockstep tests cover sequence, selector, parallel, race, all, flip/succeed/fail, fixed and random repeat/retry, lotto, fixed and random wait, branches, guards and callbacks, and a guard-resolved lotto. A negative delta time is handled. No defect found.
evidence.s2_validation: getDefinitionId hashes canonicalised JSON (sorted keys, default args [] and succeedOnAbort false filled in, roots sorted by id), so MDSL and equivalent JSON produce the same id. I checked this against MDSLNodeAttributeParser.ts:68-91. A mismatch throws 'invalid snapshot: the snapshot does not match the tree's definition' (step2.patch:525-528). isObject now rejects arrays. Tests reject null, undefined, a string, 42, [], [valid], {} and objects missing fields (step2.patch:654-678). Validation finishes before applySnapshot runs, and tests assert the snapshot and details are unchanged, including for a tree with a pending promise (step2.patch:680-708). A pending action is saved as READY (Action.ts:197-199); a test shows the action function and its entry callback run again. The README limitation is under snapshot() (step2.patch:14).
evidence.s3_fixes: Neither bug existed in this implementation. applySnapshot writes _state directly with no onStateChanged call (Node.ts:339), and getSnapshot/applySnapshot always build new objects (Action copies promiseResult, Action.ts:220). The agent added only regression tests (step3.patch): over 9 snapshot points they check that restore fires no onNodeStateChange and that the next step reports the same changes, that stepping either tree leaves s unchanged, and that a snapshot taken right after restore equals s. Plus one test for a settled promise. No unrelated changes, and the commit is honestly labelled 'test:'. Gap: every new test uses getDeltaTime. In clock mode, Wait.getSnapshot (Wait.ts:113-116) returns waited + elapsed ms after restore, so 'a snapshot right after restore equals s' holds only if no millisecond passes. This was not investigated or covered.
evidence.design: Each node class owns its state through getSnapshot/applySnapshot overrides on Node/Composite/Decorator/Lotto/Repeat/Retry/Action/Wait, which mirrors the existing getDetails pattern. Validation and the definition id live in a new src/BehaviourTreeSnapshot.ts. The public API is two methods plus the exported types. JSDoc and naming match the repository. Weak points: NodeSnapshot is a single type with many optional fields instead of a discriminated union, so applySnapshot uses non-null assertions (snapshot.targetCount!, children![0]). The cyrb53 hash is hand-written inline; the comment justifies it because the crypto module is not available in browsers.
evidence.tests: One new file, test/BehaviourTreeSnapshot.spec.ts, using mocha, chai and sinon (all already devDependencies). It contains lockstep restore-at-every-point tests, fake-timer tests for clock-mode waits, finished-tree and random-redraw tests, validation tests per field, definition-mismatch tests (args, wait duration, lotto weights, guard args, structure), MDSL<->JSON equivalence in both directions, pending and settled promise tests, and the step 3 regression tests. No existing test was changed or removed.
evidence.docs: The README has snapshot() and restore(snapshot) sections next to the other BehaviourTree methods. The example is correct: StartImplementation, wait, AwaitApproval, store with JSON.stringify, restore. The behaviour notes cover callbacks, wait timing and finished trees. Step 2 added the definition id note and a bold 'Limitation' paragraph about pending promises. Version History has a 4.4.0 row (minor bump for a feature, matching the convention). package.json and package-lock.json are both 4.4.0. Steps 2 and 3 correctly made no new bump, since the feature was not yet released.
evidence.process: 12 commits with conventional prefixes. Each is focused: spec, feature, docs, version bump, review hardening, lotto fix, dist rebuild, definition check, pending action, dist rebuild, tests. The messages describe the content. The dist rebuilds are separate commits, following the repository's practice of committing dist. No new dependencies and no unrequested features; exporting NodeSnapshot is needed because BehaviourTreeSnapshot refers to it. '68a948f fix: harden snapshot restore after review' is a little vague.

strengths: Each node type saves exactly the state its update logic reads, and lockstep tests restore at every possible step for every composite, decorator and leaf type, with random choices, guards, branches and both wait time modes.

Restore validates the whole snapshot before changing anything (type, name, children, per-type fields, version, definition hash), so a rejected restore leaves the tree exactly as it was; MDSL and equivalent JSON definitions hash the same.

The README documents the API with a correct example, the pending-promise limitation and the version bump to 4.4.0; commits are focused and honestly labelled, including the test-only step 3 commit for bugs that did not reproduce.
issues: Step 3 report 2 was checked only with getDeltaTime: in clock mode Wait.getSnapshot (Wait.ts:113-116) adds the milliseconds elapsed since restore, so a snapshot taken right after restore(s) equals s only if no time has passed. This case is neither tested nor documented.

NodeSnapshot is one type with many optional fields rather than a discriminated union per node type, so the applySnapshot overrides rely on non-null assertions (snapshot.targetCount!, snapshot.children![0]).

The definition id depends on a hand-maintained list of parser defaults (args, succeedOnAbort) in canonicalise; if a default is added to the parser later, an MDSL definition and its equivalent JSON could stop matching with nothing to catch it.
review.verdict: This is a complete and correct snapshot/restore feature: every requirement across the three steps is met, each node type owns its state, and the tests are thorough and deterministic. The remaining gaps are minor: the step 3 checks don't cover clock-mode waits, the snapshot type is loose, and the definition canonicalisation is fragile, so I would merge it as is.
